audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $617.893 million latest filed balance; $4.31 per share gross, equal to 7.1%, 4.6%, and 4.1% of bear, base, and bull equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Redemption payments reduce the equity bridge, while the additional subsidiary earnings acquired upon redemption increase future parent-attributable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of October 31, 2025, management’s estimate of the aggregate Redemption Amount of all Put Rights that we could be required to pay is approximately $467.4 million, which is included within redeemable noncontrolling interests in our Consolidated Balance Sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission from the model is demonstrated and the latest claim is larger than the cited fiscal-2025 amount. Its gross scale is material, particularly to the bear case. The net valuation error remains unresolved because deducting the obligation without adding the acquired earnings would be incomplete.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest subsidiary-level put schedule through fiscal 2036, match each payment with the earnings interest acquired, and rerun the valuation using the resulting dated cash flows and parent-attributable OE.

audit_findings.title: The owner-earnings numerator and parent share denominator may describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed NCI income was $50.137 million for the first nine months of fiscal 2026, 7.1% of $709.565 million consolidated net income
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A add-backs can overstate parent OE, while consolidated capital expenditure and working-capital deductions can understate it; consolidated cash may also exceed the parent-owned amount represented by the share denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests relates to the 20% noncontrolling interest held by Lufthansa Technik AG in HEICO Aerospace Holdings Corp. and the noncontrolling interests held by others in certain subsidiaries of the FSG and ETG.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated if, as reported, parent-attributable income was combined with consolidated cash-flow adjustments. The greater-than-5% NCI scale makes the issue reasonably capable of affecting value, but the record does not establish the net direction or amount because the relevant subsidiary allocations are missing.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE year using parent-attributable D&A, capital expenditure, working capital, and excess cash; alternatively rebuild a fully consolidated valuation and deduct both redeemable and permanent NCI claims explicitly.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven growth may be capitalized without paying for acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed acquisition outlays were $2,421.788 million in fiscal 2023, $219.293 million in fiscal 2024, $629.828 million in fiscal 2025, and $1,018.164 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter the historical OE trend and forecast growth, while acquisition consideration is excluded from OE reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions have been an important element of our growth strategy over the past thirty-five years, supplementing our organic growth.
audit_findings.explanation: Acquisition dependence and the exclusion of acquisition spending are demonstrated. A valuation overstatement is not yet demonstrated because recent reported organic sales growth exceeded the selected 8%-10% rates, but sales growth does not establish organic OE growth or its durability. Given the size and frequency of acquisitions and the valuation's sensitivity to growth, the unresolved adjustment is reasonably capable of changing value materially.
audit_findings.action: Construct an organic-versus-acquired OE history, determine sustainable organic OE growth, estimate the normalized acquisition spending required for any incremental forecast growth, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Adding back acquired-intangible amortization may conceal economic asset depletion
audit_findings.magnitude: $137.9 million fiscal-2025 amortization add-back exposure, equal to 19.3% of the $713.0 million anchor; the economic depletion portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economically recurring portion of acquired-intangible amortization should reduce normalized OE or be represented by maintenance acquisition, customer-retention, technology-renewal, or development spending.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization expense related to intangible assets was $ 137.9 million, $ 122.3 million and $ 85.9 million in fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The full amortization add-back is demonstrated, but economic depletion is only an unresolved possibility because HEICO also expenses substantial R&D and selling activity that may maintain these assets. The exposed amount is large enough that even a partial economic charge could materially affect the OE anchor and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Map amortization by asset class and acquisition, test whether expensed R&D and selling costs maintain the associated customer and technology assets, and rerun sensitivities for the supported economic-amortization or maintenance-spending charge.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $69.097 million latest filed liability; $0.48 per share, equal to 0.8%, 0.5%, and 0.5% of bear, base, and bull equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreflected contingent consideration is a bridge liability, although earnings already include some fair-value remeasurement expense and cash-flow statements classify associated payments separately.
audit_findings.evidence: As of October 31, 2025 and 2024, $46.2 million and $30.2 million of contingent consideration was accrued within our Consolidated Balance Sheets, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest liability is absent from the stated bridge, but deducting the entire filed fair value would reduce every scenario by only about $0.48 per share and less than 1%. That scale cannot alter the valuation conclusion, and the true adjustment may be smaller after avoiding double counting.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $40.102 million current and $28.995 million long-term balances to OE remeasurements and prior payments, then disclose or deduct only the unreflected amount in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Discrete option-exercise tax benefits may inflate normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.2 million fiscal-2025 benefit, equal to 3.4% of $806.3 million latest OE and 3.8% of the $713.0 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The discrete benefits increase net income and therefore historical OE, potentially lifting the fitted trend anchor; option exercises also affect dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognized a discrete tax benefit from stock option exercises in the first quarter of fiscal 2025 and 2024 of $27.2 million and $13.6 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefits and absence of an explicit normalization are demonstrated, although their sustainable level is unresolved. Even the full fiscal-2025 benefit is below 4% of the relevant OE measures, and its effect on a ten-year fitted trend should be smaller than a direct one-for-one anchor reduction. This cannot close the large gap between the $104.28 bull value and the $325.48 market price.
audit_findings.action: Remove or normalize the fiscal-2023 through fiscal-2026 discrete benefits, recompute the historical OE series and log-trend anchor, and confirm consistency with the fully diluted share assumption.
